flawed_step: Conditioning only on X_n can average out information retained in the full history (X_1,...,X_n), so E[X_{n+1}|X_n]=X_n does not imply E[X_{n+1}|F_n]=X_n.
counterexample: Take four equiprobable outcomes with (X_1,X_2,X_3) equal to (1,0,1), (1,2,2), (-1,0,-1), and (-1,-2,-2). Then E[X_2|X_1=1]=1 and E[X_2|X_1=-1]=-1. Also, conditional on X_2=0, X_3 is equally likely to be 1 or -1, so E[X_3|X_2=0]=0; for X_2=2 or -2, X_3=X_2. Hence E[X_3|X_2]=X_2. However, X_3 is determined by (X_1,X_2), and on the event (X_1,X_2)=(1,0), E[X_3|F_2]=1 != 0=X_2 (similarly for (-1,0)). Thus the process is not a martingale in its natural filtration.
assessment_summary: A finite, integrable four-outcome process satisfies both stated current-value conditional-expectation identities but fails the martingale identity at time 2.
